title: Fixed Transverse Drum and Paired Inclined Rack Gate
description: One wholly newly authored complete fixed roller-gate-inspired exterior over a full dry open channel. One entire closed transverse cylindrical barrier remains raised above the floor. Two full short end journals connect that drum to two whole thick cog exteriors, each supported at a separate complete inclined toothed rack on its own whole rising pier. One continuous full channel floor and low side banks root both complete pier-and-rack stations. A closed side hoist-case exterior and one uninterrupted fixed haul-line appearance join the right-hand assembly. The entire cog and each complete rack carry coarse blunt geometric teeth, not textures or loose tooth pieces, and all components are connected through finite fixed overlap witnesses. Unlike the old radial gate there is no thin partial cylindrical leaf, inner curved rib or triangular arm system converging at rear pivots: the broad full cylinder and coaxial end cogs sit directly at inclined distributed side tracks. Unlike the paired davit guides there are no curved cheek bays, bent outboard arms, suspended empty eyes or common H-frame. All numeric profiles, teeth, drum, piers and channel are independently authored; no gate, roller, cog, rack, crane or channel mesh imported or extracted. Four opaque constant untextured PBR materials, metres Z up, whole horizontal envelope centred on the finite full channel ground sole, one whole prop zero scenes. Simplified empty fixed machinery-architecture art only, not an engineering section or working gate. Teeth deliberately overlap for the shown static support and are not a meshing profile; the haul line is a coarse continuous closed solid, not articulated chain links or a validated reeving path. No water, seal, hoist internals, rotation, rolling travel, tooth engagement, synchronized motion, force, torque, pressure, water retention, hydraulic control, loading, access, manufacture, installation or equipment/civil safety capability made or verified. No animation, rigging or interaction.
